Surah al-Ra'd is Meccan. It has forty-three verses according to the Kufan count and forty-five according to the Syrian count.

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿Alif-Lam-Mim-Ra.﴾ "I am Allah, the All-Knowing, the All-Seeing." This is related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him. ﴿Those﴾ is a reference to the verses of the surah. ﴿are the verses of the Book.﴾ By "the Book" is meant the surah; that is, "those verses are the verses of the complete and wondrous surah in its genre." ﴿And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾ means the entire Qur'an. ﴿is the truth﴾ is the predicate of "that which" (alladhi). ﴿But most of the people do not believe﴾ so they say, "Muhammad has fabricated it."

Then he mentioned what makes faith obligatory, saying: ﴿Allah is He who raised the heavens﴾ — i.e., He created them raised up, not placed low, and then He raised them. "Allah" is the subject (mubtada'), and the predicate (khabar) is "who raised the heavens." ﴿Without pillars﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal), and ʿamad is the plural of ʿimad or ʿamud (pillar). ﴿You see them﴾ — the pronoun refers back to "the heavens," meaning: you see them thus, so there is no need for clarification; or it refers to ʿamad, in which case it occupies a genitive position as an attribute (sifah) of ʿamad, meaning: without pillars that are visible. ﴿Then He established Himself upon the Throne﴾ — He took possession of it (istawla) through power and the enforcement of authority. ﴿And He subjected the sun and the moon﴾ — for the benefits of His servants and the welfare of His lands. ﴿Each runs for a specified term﴾ — and that is the ending of the world. ﴿He arranges the affair﴾ — the affair of His dominion (malakut) and lordship (rububiyyah). ﴿He details the signs﴾ — He makes clear His signs in His revealed Books. ﴿That you may be certain of the meeting with your Lord﴾ — that you may be certain that this Arranger and Detailer is one to whom you must return. (p-142)

And He it is who spread out the earth (بَسَطَها, He spread it out), and placed therein firm mountains (جِبالًا ثَوابِتَ) and rivers (جارِيَةً, flowing). And of all fruits He made therein two mates, two (زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ), i.e., black and white, sweet and sour, small and large, and what is similar to that. He covers (يُغْشِي) the night over the day (يُلْبِسُهُ مَكانَهُ, He clothes it in its place), so that it becomes black and dark after having been white and bright. Ḥamzah, ʿAlī and Abū Bakr read "yughashshī" (يُغَشِّي). Surely in that are signs for a people who reflect (يَتَفَكَّرُونَ), so that they know that it has a Creator who is All-Knowing, Wise, Powerful.

And on the earth are adjoining tracts: gardens of vines, and tilled land, and palm trees, some multiple-trunked and some single-trunked, all watered with one water; yet We make some of them excel others in fruit. Indeed in that are signs for a people who use their reason.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 4:

﴿وَفِي الأرْضِ قِطَعٌ مُتَجاوِراتٌ﴾ "And on the earth are adjoining tracts" — plots of different kinds, though adjoining and touching one another: good land next to salt-marsh (sabkha), fertile land next to barren (zahida), hard land next to soft. That is a proof of a Capable, Governing, Willing Agent who places His acts in one way and not in another. ﴿وَجَنّاتٌ﴾ "And gardens" is conjoined to "qit'un" (tracts). ﴿مِن أعْنابٍ وزَرْعٌ ونَخِيلٌ صِنْوانٌ وغَيْرُ صِنْوانٍ﴾ "Of vines, and tilled crops, and palm trees, some multiple-trunked and some single-trunked." With the nominative (raf'): Makki, Basri and Hafs read it so, as a conjunction to "qit'un." Others read it in the genitive (jarr), by conjunction to "a'nab" (vines). "Sinwan" is the plural of "sinw," which is a palm that has two heads but a single root. From Hafs, it is also read with a damma on the "sad," and both are dialect forms (lughatan). ﴿يُسْقى بِماءٍ واحِدٍ﴾ "Watered with one water." With the "ya" (yusqa): 'Asim and Shami. ﴿وَنُفَضِّلُ بَعْضَها عَلى بَعْضٍ﴾ "Yet We make some of them excel others." With the "ya" (nufaddilu): Hamza and Ali. ﴿فِي الأُكُلِ﴾ "In the fruit," that is, in the produce (al-thamar). With the kaf sukun (al-ukl): Nafi' and Makki. ﴿إنَّ في ذَلِكَ لآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ "Indeed in that are signs for a people who use their reason." From al-Hasan: he likened the differences of hearts in their effects, their lights and their secrets to the differences of the tracts in their rivers, their flowers and their fruits.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 5:

﴿And if you are astonished﴾ O Muhammad, at their saying in denial of the Resurrection, ﴿then astonishing is their saying﴾. (p-143) It is a predicate and a subject, meaning: their saying is truly deserving of being wondered at, because the One who has power to originate what He has enumerated for you, then repeating it is the easiest and simplest thing for Him. So their denial is one of the marvels among marvels. ﴿When we are dust, shall we indeed be in a new creation?﴾ It is in the place of nominative case as a substitute (badal) for "their saying." ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah each read it with two hamzahs (ʾa-ʾa). ﴿Those are the ones who disbelieved in their Lord﴾: "those" refers to the disbelievers who persist in their disbelief. ﴿And those, the shackles are around their necks﴾: this is a description of them as persistent in obstinacy, or it is part of the threat. ﴿And those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever﴾: the repetition of "those" indicates the magnification of the matter.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 6:

﴿And they ask you to hasten the evil before the good﴾ — that is, the punishment before the well-being. The reason is that they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to bring them the punishment, mocking his warning.

﴿And indeed exemplary punishments (al-mathulat) have passed before them﴾ — that is, the punishments inflicted on their likes among the deniers. So why do they not take heed from them, so that they would not mock? The word mathula (exemplary punishment) denotes a punishment because of the resemblance between the punishment and the one punished for.

﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it﴾ [al-Shura: 40]. ﴿And indeed your Lord is full of forgiveness for mankind despite their wrongdoing﴾ — that is, along with their wronging themselves through sins. The phrase ʿalā ẓulmihim is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: while they are wronging themselves. Al-Suddi said: "It refers to the believers. This is the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah, since it mentions forgiveness together with wrongdoing, and this is without repentance, for repentance removes and lifts it." ﴿And indeed your Lord is severe in punishment﴾ — against the disbelievers. Or both apply to the believers, but it is contingent upon His will in both cases; that is, He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 7:

﴿And those who disbelieve say: "Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?"﴾ They did not count the signs that were sent down upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as proofs, out of obstinacy, and so they proposed the like of the signs of Musa and Isa: the transformation of the staff into a serpent, and the raising of the dead. Then it was said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿You are only a warner﴾. That is: you are only a man whom We have sent as a warner, one who frightens them of the evil consequence and who gives them sincere advice, like the other Messengers. (p-144) It is not incumbent upon you except to bring that by which it becomes valid that you are a warning Messenger, and the validity of that is achieved by any sign whatsoever; all the signs are equal in achieving the validity of the claim by them. ﴿And for every people there is a guide﴾: from among the Prophets, who guides them to the religion and calls them to Allah with a sign specific to him, not with what they desire and dictate.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 8:

﴿Allah knows what every female carries, and what the wombs diminish and what they increase.﴾ What (ما) in these three places is a relative pronoun (mawsulah), meaning: He knows what she carries of the offspring, in whatever state it is, whether male or female, complete or incomplete (khadaj), beautiful or ugly, tall or short, and other than that. "And what the wombs diminish" means: and He knows what they lose; it is said: "ghada al-ma'u" and "ghadtuhu ana" (the water subsided, and I caused it to subside). "And what they increase" means: the number of offspring, for it may contain one, two, three or four; or the body of the offspring, for it may be complete or incomplete; or the duration of the pregnancy, for it may be less than nine months and may extend beyond that to two years according to us (the Hanafis), to four years according to al-Shafi'i, and to five years according to Malik. Or (ما) may be a verbal-noun particle (masdariyyah), meaning: He knows the carrying of every female, and He knows the diminishing and increasing of the wombs.

﴿And everything with Him is by a measure﴾, that is, by a determined amount and limit that it neither exceeds nor falls short of, in accordance with His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have created everything according to a measure﴾ [al-Qamar: 49].

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 9:

﴿The Knower of the unseen﴾: what is hidden from creation. ﴿And the visible﴾: what they have witnessed. ﴿The Great﴾: the One of supreme rank, before whom everything is lesser. ﴿The Exalted﴾: the One who is elevated above everything by His power; or the One who is too great for the attributes of created beings and exalted above them. And reading it with a yāʾ (ي) in both cases [i.e., al-Mutaʿālī with yāʾ rather than the wāw-form] is attributed to Ibn Kathīr of Mecca (Makkī).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 10:

﴿It is the same for you, whether one of you conceals speech or openly declares it﴾, i.e., in His knowledge. ﴿And whoever is hidden by the night﴾, concealed, ﴿and goes about freely by day﴾, i.e., goes forth on his path (sarb), that is, on his way and direction. It is said: "sariba fi al-ard suruban" (he went about in the land). "Wa sarib" is a conjunction (ʿatf) upon "man huwa mustakhfin" (whoever is hidden), not upon "mustakhfin" (hidden), or upon "mustakhfin", except that "man" carries the meaning of the dual.

The pronoun in ﴿لَهُ﴾ refers back to "man" (مَن), as if it were said: for whoever conceals speech, whoever speaks openly, whoever hides himself, and whoever goes forth openly. ﴿مُعَقِّباتٌ﴾ means groups of angels who succeed one another in guarding him. The original form is مُعْتَقِبات, and the ta' was assimilated into the qaf. Alternatively, it is مُفْعِلات, from عَقِبَه, meaning he came upon his heels (عَقِب), because some of them follow others, or because they record what is spoken and write it down.

﴿مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ ومِن خَلْفِهِ﴾ means: in front of him and behind him.

﴿يَحْفَظُونَهُ مِن أمْرِ اللهِ﴾: both are attributes together, and "from the command of Allah" is not a complement of "guard." It is as if it were said: "for him are successive [angels] by the command of Allah." Or: they guard him by reason of the command of Allah, meaning because Allah the Exalted commanded them to guard him. Or: they guard him from the punishment and vengeance of Allah when he sins, through their supplication for him.

﴿إنَّ اللهَ لا يُغَيِّرُ ما بِقَوْمٍ﴾ of well-being and blessing ﴿حَتّى يُغَيِّرُوا ما بِأنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ of a good state, through the abundance of sins.

﴿وَإذا أرادَ اللهُ بِقَوْمٍ سُوءًا﴾ meaning punishment, ﴿فَلا مَرَدَّ لَهُ﴾ so nothing repels it, ﴿وَما لَهم مِن دُونِهِ مِن والٍ﴾ and they have no protector apart from Allah, from among those who manage their affairs and repel [harm] from them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 12:

﴿He it is who shows you the lightning, [causing] fear and hope.﴾ Both [khawfan and tam'an] are in the accusative as *ḥāl* (circumstantial accusative) from "al-barq" (the lightning), as if it itself were fear and hope; or [they are in the accusative] as [describing] "dhā khawfin wa dhā ṭam'in" (possessors of fear and possessors of hope); or [they are a *ḥāl*] from the addressees, meaning: fearful and hopeful. The meaning is: one fears the falling of thunderbolts at the flash of lightning, and hopes for the rain. Abū al-Ṭayyib said:

؎ A youth like the dark clouds: he is feared and hoped for; from him the rain is hoped for, and from him the thunderbolts are feared.

(p. 146) Or [it means] one fears the rain who is harmed by it, like the traveller and one who has no house to shelter him; and among lands are those whose people do not benefit from rain, like the people of Egypt. And one hopes for it who gains benefit from it. ﴿And He produces the clouds﴾: "al-sahāb" is a *ism jins* (collective noun), and its singular is "saḥāba." ﴿The heavy﴾: with water. It is the plural of "thaqīla" (feminine of heavy); one says "saḥāba thaqīla" (a heavy cloud) and "saḥāb thiqāl" (heavy clouds).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 13:

﴿And the thunder glorifies [Him] with His praise﴾. It is said: the hearers of the thunder among the servants who hope for rain glorify [Him], that is, they cry out, "Glory be to Allah" and "Praise be to Allah." It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The thunder is an angel appointed over the clouds, with him are whips of fire with which he drives the clouds, and the sound that is heard is his driving of the clouds until it reaches where it was commanded."

﴿And the angels, out of fear of Him﴾: the angels glorify [Him] out of their awe and reverence for Him.

﴿And He sends the thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills﴾. The ṣāʿiqah (thunderbolt) is fire that falls from the sky. When He mentioned His all-pervading knowledge of everything, and the equality in His sight of the manifest and the hidden, and what indicates His overwhelming power and His oneness, He said: ﴿Yet they dispute about Allah﴾. That is, those who denied the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) dispute about Allah, in that they reject what he ascribes to Him of power to resurrect and recreate the creatures, by their saying, "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?" and they deny His oneness by taking partners, and they attribute to Him being one of the bodies by their saying, "The angels are the daughters of Allah." Or the waw is for the state (ḥāl), meaning: He strikes with them whom He wills while they are disputing.

That is because Arbad (brother of Labid ibn Rabiʿah al-ʿĀmirī) said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he came as a delegation to him with ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl, intending to kill him, so Allah struck ʿĀmir with a boil like the boil of a camel and death in the house of a woman of Salūl, and sent a thunderbolt upon Arbad, which killed him: "Tell me about our Lord, is He of copper or of iron?"

﴿And He is severe in might﴾: that is, al-miḥāl is al-mumāḥalah, which is severity of cunning and plotting. From it comes taḥammala li-kadhā (he exerted himself to contrive it, when he strained to use a stratagem and laboured at it), and maḥala bi-fulān (he plotted against someone and carried tales of him to the ruler). The meaning is that He is severe in cunning and plotting against His enemies, bringing destruction upon them from where they do not perceive.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 14:

﴿To Him is the call of truth﴾ The word "call" is attributed to "truth," which is the opposite of falsehood (batil), to indicate that the calling is connected with truth and is far removed from falsehood. The meaning is that Allah, glory be to Him, is called upon, so He responds to the call and gives the one who calls what he asks for. Thus it is a call connected with truth, because He is truly deserving that supplication be directed to Him, since there is benefit and profit in calling upon Him, unlike those whose supplication brings no benefit and yields no result.

The connection of "Severe in might" and "To Him is the call of truth" with what precedes them, regarding the story of Arbad, is clear, because his being struck by the thunderbolt was a "might" (mihal) from Allah and a plot against him from a direction he did not perceive. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had invoked against him and his companion, saying: "O Allah, cause them to be swallowed up by the earth in whatever way You will," and it was answered concerning them, so the call was a call of truth. According to the first interpretation, it is also a warning to the disbelievers for their disputing with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), with the descent of His might upon them, and with the answering of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) call against them if he invokes against them.

﴿And those they call upon besides Him﴾ besides Allah ﴿do not respond to them with anything﴾ of their requests ﴿except as one who stretches out his hands to water that it may reach his mouth﴾. This is an exception from the verbal noun: that is, from the response indicated by "do not respond," because the verb, by its letters, indicates the verbal noun, by its form indicates the time, and by necessity indicates the place and state. So it is permissible to make an exception from each of these from the verb. The sense thus becomes: they do not respond with a response except a response like the response of one who stretches out his hands to water, that is, like the response of water to one who stretches out his hands toward it, asking that it reach his mouth. Water is inanimate; it does not perceive the stretching out of his hands, nor his thirst and need for it, and it cannot answer his supplication and reach his mouth. Likewise, those they call upon are inanimate; they do not sense their supplication, cannot respond to them, and have no power to benefit them. The "lam" in "that it may reach" is connected to "stretches out his hands."

﴿And it is not one who will reach it﴾: and the water does not reach his mouth. ﴿And the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error﴾: in loss, with no benefit in it, for if they call upon Allah He does not answer them, and if they call upon the idols, the idols cannot respond to them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 15:

﴿And to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and the earth﴾, a prostration of worship and submission, ﴿willingly﴾ (a circumstantial qualifier, ḥāl), meaning the angels and the believers, ﴿and unwillingly﴾, meaning the hypocrites and the disbelievers in a state of hardship and distress. ﴿And their shadows﴾ is conjoined to "man" (man, "whoever"). It is the plural of ẓill (shadow). ﴿In the mornings﴾ is the plural of ghadāt (ghadāh, morning), like qunī and qanāh (qanāh, reed-shaft). ﴿And the evenings﴾ is the plural of uṣul, which is the plural of aṣīl (evening). It is said: the shadow of everything prostrates to Allah in the mornings and evenings. The shadow of the disbeliever prostrates unwillingly, while he is unwilling, and the shadow of the believer prostrates willingly, while he is willing.

**Al-Nasafi, *Madarik al-Tanzil*, on Surah 13, verse 16:**

﴿Say: "Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?" Say: "Allah."﴾ This is a recounting of their own acknowledgment, for when he says to them, "Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?", they have no choice but to say, "Allah." Its proof is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy: "They say, 'Allah.'" Or it is *talqin* (prompting, supplying the answer), meaning: if they do not answer, then prompt them, for there is no answer except this. ﴿Say: "Have you then taken, apart from Him, protectors?"﴾ After you have known Him to be the Lord of the heavens and the earth, have you taken other gods apart from Him? ﴿who possess not for themselves any benefit or harm﴾ They are unable to bring benefit to themselves or to ward off harm from themselves, so how could they be able to do so for others, when you have preferred them over the Creator, the Provider, the Rewarder, and the Punisher? How clear is your error! ﴿Say: "Are the blind and the seeing equal?"﴾ That is, the disbeliever and the believer, or one who sees something and one to whom nothing is hidden. ﴿Or are the darknesses and the light equal?﴾ That is, the creeds of disbelief and of faith. "Equal" (*yastawi*) is read by the Kufans except Hafs. ﴿Or have they set up for God partners who have created like His creation?﴾ Rather, have they set up... The *hamza* here carries the sense of denunciation. ﴿who created as He created﴾ They created the like of His creation. This clause describes "partners," meaning: they did not take for God partners who are creators, when they have created the like of God's creation. ﴿So the creation became confused for them﴾ So God's creation was confused for them with the creation of the partners, so that they would say, "These have the power to create just as God has the power," and so deserve worship, and we therefore take them as partners to Him and worship them as He is worshipped. But they have taken for Him partners who are powerless, who cannot do what creation can do, let alone what the Creator can do. ﴿Say: "Allah is the Creator of all things."﴾ That is, the Creator of bodies and accidents; there is no creator other than God, and it is not correct that He should have a partner in creation, and therefore He has no partner in worship. Whoever says that God did not create the actions of creatures, and that they created them themselves, then in their view creation has become confused. ﴿And He is the One, the Unique﴾ Singular in lordship. ﴿the Subduer﴾ None can overcome Him, and all else is subject to lordship and subjugation.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 17:**

﴿Sent down﴾ [al-Ra'd: 7], that is, the One, the Subduer, who is God, glorified is He, ﴿from the sky﴾, from the clouds, ﴿water﴾, rain. ﴿So the valleys flowed﴾: plural of *wadi* (valley), which is the place where water flows in abundance. It is indefinite (*nakkara*) because rain does not come except in rotation among the lands, so some flow while others do not. ﴿According to its measure﴾, according to the quantity that God knows to be beneficial to those upon whom it rains and not harmful. ﴿The torrent carried﴾, that is, it lifted up, ﴿foam﴾, which is the froth that rises on the surface of the water, the meaning being that foam covered it. ﴿Swelling﴾, puffed up and raised above the surface of the torrent. ﴿And from that which they kindle﴾ (the reading with *ya'* is that of the Kufans except Abu Bakr; *min* here is for the beginning of the extent, that is, from it arises foam like the foam of water; or it is partitive, that is, some of it is foam) ﴿in the fire﴾ is a circumstantial state (*hal*, a clause describing the condition of the subject at the time of the action) of the pronoun in "upon it," that is, that which you kindle upon it, existing in the fire. ﴿Seeking ornament﴾, seeking an ornament; it is a verbal noun in the position of a *hal* relative to "you kindle." ﴿Or goods﴾ of iron, copper and lead, from which vessels are made and that which is enjoyed at home and on journeys; it is conjoined to "ornament," that is, an adornment of gold and silver. ﴿Foam﴾, dross (*khabath*, impurities), and it is the subject (*mubtada'*). ﴿Like it﴾ is a qualifier (*na't*) of it, and "and from that which you kindle" is its predicate (*khabar*), that is, from these metals, when they are melted, there is foam like the foam of water. ﴿Thus God strikes the truth and falsehood﴾, that is, the likeness of truth and falsehood. ﴿As for the foam, it passes away as scum﴾ is a circumstantial state, that is, dissipating. It is what the cooking pot throws off when it boils and what the sea throws off at its surging. *Al-jafa'* means casting away; *jafa'tu al-rajul* means I threw the man down. ﴿And as for that which benefits people﴾, of water, ornaments and vessels, ﴿it remains in the earth﴾: the water settles in springs, wells, grains and fruits, and likewise jewels remain in the earth for a long period. ﴿Thus God strikes the parables﴾, so that the truth may become distinct from falsehood.

It was also said: this is a parable that God struck for truth and its people, and for falsehood and its party. He likened truth and its people to the water that descends from the sky, by which the valleys of people flow, so they live by it and it benefits them in various kinds of benefit; and to the metal which they use in fashioning ornaments from it and making vessels and various implements. That remains in the earth, enduring with an evident permanence, the water settling in its benefits. Likewise jewels remain for lengthy periods. He likened falsehood, in the swiftness of its vanishing and the imminence of its removal, to the foam of the torrent which is cast away, and to the foam of the metal which floats on top of it when it is melted.

The majority said: this is a parable that God, exalted is He, struck for the Qur'an, the hearts, truth and falsehood. The water is the Qur'an, which was sent down for the life of hearts as water is for bodies; the valleys are the hearts; and the meaning of "according to its measure" is according to the breadth of the heart and its narrowness. The foam is the whisperings of the soul and the insinuations of Satan. The pure water which is beneficial is like truth. Just as the foam goes away as falsehood while the purity of the water remains, so likewise the whisperings of the soul and the insinuations of Satan go away, and the truth remains as it is. As for the ornament of gold and silver, it is a parable for noble states and pure morals. As for the goods of iron, copper and lead, it is a parable for deeds prepared with sincerity and readied for deliverance, for deeds bring reward and repel punishment, just as some of those substances are instruments of benefit for earning and some are tools of defense in war. As for the foam, it is showing off, heedlessness, weariness and laziness.

(p-150)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 18:

The lam in ﴿for those who responded﴾ (li-lladhina istajabu), meaning "those who answered," is connected to "yadribu" (He sets forth), meaning: "Thus does Allah set forth the parables" (p-151) for the believers who responded ﴿to their Lord is the best (reward)﴾ (li-rabbihim al-husna). The word "al-husna" is an adjective of the verbal noun of "istajabu," meaning: they responded with the best response. ﴿And those who did not respond to Him﴾ (wa-lladhina lam yastajibu lahu), meaning: and for the disbelievers who did not respond. These two are the two parables of the two groups.

His saying ﴿if they had all that is in the earth entirely, and the like of it with it, they would surely ransom themselves with it﴾ (law anna lahum ma fi al-ardi jami'an wa-mithlahu ma'ahu la-ftadaw bihi) is a independent statement mentioning what has been prepared for those who did not respond. Meaning: even if they possessed all the wealth of this world and possessed along with it the like of it, they would surely spend it in order to ward off the punishment of Allah from themselves.

The view is that the speech is complete at "al-amthal" (the parables), and what follows is a new statement. "Al-husna" is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate (khabar) is "lilladhina istajabu," and the meaning is: for them is the best reward, which is Paradise. "Wa-lladhina lam yastajibu" is a subject whose predicate is "law" together with what is in its scope.

﴿Those, for them is the evil of the reckoning﴾ (ulaika lahum su'u al-hisab). The discussion of it (al-munaqasha fihi), in the hadith: "Whoever is called to account in detail is punished" (man nuqisha al-hisab 'uzziba).

﴿And their refuge is Hell﴾ (wa-ma'wahum jahannam), and their return after the reckoning is the Fire. ﴿And wretched is the resting place﴾ (wa-bi'sa al-mihad): the place that is prepared; the thing being condemned is omitted, meaning: Hell.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 19:

The interrogative hamzah of denial (hamzat al-inkar) has entered upon the fa' in ﴿Is then he who knows﴾, to deny that any doubt could arise after the parable that has been struck, regarding the state of one who knows ﴿that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth﴾, and so responds, being far removed from the state of the ignorant one who has not gained insight and therefore does not respond. This is what is meant by His words ﴿as one who is blind﴾, [the distance is] like the distance between the scum (al-zabad) and the water, and between the dross (al-khabath) and the refined gold (al-ibriz). ﴿Only those of understanding are mindful﴾, i.e., those who act upon the dictates of their intellects, so they reflect and gain insight.

Those who fulfil the covenant of God (﴿الَّذِينَ يُوفُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللهِ﴾) is the subject (mubtada'), and the predicate (khabar) is "those, for them is the good end of the abode" (﴿أُولَئِكَ لَهم عُقْبى الدارِ﴾), like His saying: ﴿And those who break the covenant of God after its binding, and who sever what God has commanded to be joined, and who cause corruption in the land — for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode.﴾ It is also said that it is an attribute (sifah) of "those of understanding" (﴿لِأُولِي الألْبابِ﴾). The first view is more preferable (awjah). The covenant of God is what they bound upon themselves of testifying to His lordship, as in His saying: ﴿And He took testimony from them against themselves: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes, we testify."﴾ (p-152) ﴿And they do not break the compact (al-mithaq)﴾: what they confirmed upon themselves and accepted of faith in God and other covenants between them and God and between them and the servants. This is a generalization after a specification (ta'mim ba'da takhsis).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 21:

﴿And those who join what Allah has commanded to be joined﴾ of the ties of kinship and relationships (al-arham wal-qarabat). It also includes maintaining the kinship of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the kinship of the believers, which is established through the bond of faith: "The believers are but brothers" (Qur'an 49:10), by doing good to them according to one's ability, supporting them, defending them, showing compassion toward them, spreading the greeting of peace among them, visiting their sick, and, among this, observing the rights of companions, servants, neighbours and travelling companions. ﴿And they fear their Lord﴾, that is, His threat in its entirety, ﴿and they dread the evil of the reckoning﴾, especially so that they take account of themselves before they are brought to account.

ﷻ "And those who are patient" — this is unrestricted as to what they bear patiently: calamities affecting their persons and their wealth, and the hardships of the obligations (taklif). "Seeking the Face of Allah" (Q. 2:272) — not in order that it be said, "How patient he is, how well he bears misfortunes and how steadfast he is at the time of upheavals!", nor so that he not be blamed for impatience. "And they establish the prayer" — they persist in maintaining it. "And they spend of what We have provided for them" — i.e., from what is lawful (ḥalāl), even though what is unlawful (ḥarām) is also a provision in Our sight — "secretly and openly." This includes voluntary (nawāfil) charity, for it is better in secret, and obligatory (farā'iḍ) charity, for to make it public is better, as it negates suspicion. "And they repel evil with good" — they counter with good speech what comes to them of the evil of others. And when they are deprived, they give; when they are wronged, they pardon; when they are cut off, they maintain ties; when they sin, they repent; when they flee, they return (in repentance to Allah); and when they see an evil, they command its change. These are eight deeds, pointing to the eight gates of Paradise. "For them is the good outcome of the abode" — the final end of the world, which is Paradise, because it is what Allah willed to be the final end of the world and the place of return for its people.

"Gardens of Eden" (jannatu ʿadnin) is in apposition (badal) to "the good end of the abode." ﴿They will enter them, and whoever was righteous﴾ — that is, who believed — ﴿among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants﴾. It is also read "ṣalaḥa" (with a different vowel), though the fatḥa (ṣalaḥa) is more eloquent. The word "man" (whoever) is in the nominative position by coordination (ʿaṭf) with the pronoun in "yadkhulūnahā" (they enter them). This is permissible even without emphasis (taʾkīd), because the object pronoun has become a separator (fāṣil). Al-Zajjaj permitted that it be an object of accompaniment (mafʿūl maʿahu). He described them with righteousness so that it would be known that lineages do not benefit by themselves. The intended meaning is the father of each one of them, as if it were said: "from their fathers and their mothers." ﴿And the angels will enter upon them from every gate﴾ — at the rate of three times every day and night, bearing gifts and glad tidings of God's good pleasure.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 24:

﴿Peace be upon you﴾ is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), since the meaning is: "saying, 'Peace be upon you,'" or "greeting [you] with peace." ﴿For that you endured﴾ is connected to an omitted element whose estimated form is: "This [is] for that you endured," i.e., this reward is because of your patience in refraining from desires, or in obedience to God's command, or [it is connected] to "peace," i.e., "We greet you and honor you for your patience." The first is more correct (awjah). ﴿How excellent is the final abode﴾: the Gardens.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 25:

﴿And those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification﴾ after they had bound themselves to it through acknowledgment and acceptance, ﴿and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined, and cause corruption on the earth﴾ through disbelief and wrongdoing. ﴿Those – for them is the curse﴾ meaning distance from mercy, ﴿and for them is the evil abode﴾. It may be meant that it is the evil outcome of this world, since it stands in contrast to the good outcome of the abode (of the Hereafter); and it may be meant by the abode Hell, and by its evil its punishment.

God extends provision to whomever He wills and restricts it. The meaning is that God alone extends provision and restricts it, not any other. ﴿And they rejoiced in the worldly life﴾ in what He had extended to them of the world, a joy of insolence and exultation, not the joy of gladness at God's grace and favor upon them. They did not meet it with thanks, so that they might be rewarded with the bliss of the Hereafter. ﴿Yet the worldly life, in comparison with the Hereafter, is but a brief enjoyment﴾. It was hidden from them that the bliss of this world, compared with the bliss of the Hereafter, is nothing but a meager thing enjoyed briefly, like the hasty snatch of a rider (ʿujlat al-rakib, a quick stop taken on a journey), which is what one hastily takes of dates or a sip of sawiq (a gruel made of toasted grain). (p-154)

And those who disbelieve say, "Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?" ﴿Say: Indeed, Allah leads astray whom He wills⁠﴾ by [their] demanding signs after the miracles have become manifest, ﴿and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance⁠﴾, and guides to His religion whoever returns to Him with his heart.

﴿Those who believe﴾ are they. Or its place is accusative, as a substitute (*badal*) for "مَن" (*man*, "those who"). ﴿And their hearts find rest﴾ are at rest ﴿in the remembrance of God﴾ constantly, or by the Qur'an, or by His promise. ﴿Surely, in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest﴾: because of His remembrance, the hearts of the believers find rest.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 29:

﴿Those who have believed and done righteous deeds﴾ is the subject (mubtada’), ﴿Ṭūbā lahum﴾ is its predicate (khabar). Ṭūbā is a verbal noun (maṣdar) from ṭāba, like bushrā. The meaning of ṭūbā laka is: you have attained good and goodness. Its place in i’rab is either the accusative or the nominative, as in your saying: ṭayyiban laka, ṭayyibun laka, and salāman laka, salāmun laka. The lām in “lahum” is for specification (lil-bayān), like it in saqyan laka. The wāw in ṭūbā is converted from a yā’ because of the ḍammah before it, like muqin. The reading in ﴿wa-ḥusnu ma’āb﴾ (and a good return), meaning a place of return, with both the nominative and the accusative, indicates its two places (in i’rab).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 30:

﴿Thus We have sent you﴾ Like that sending (of earlier messengers), We have sent you with a sending that has distinction and excellence over all other sendings. Then he explained how He sent him, saying: ﴿to a community before which other communities have passed away﴾, i.e., We have sent you to a community that was preceded by many communities, so it is the last of the communities, and you are the seal of the prophets. ﴿So that you may recite to them that which We have revealed to you﴾, i.e., so that you may read to them the Great Book which We have revealed to you. ﴿And they disbelieve﴾: the condition of these people is that they disbelieve ﴿in the Most Merciful﴾, the One of far-reaching mercy whose mercy encompasses everything. ﴿Say: He is my Lord﴾, the Lord of everything. ﴿There is no deity except Him﴾, i.e., He is my Lord, the One, exalted above partners. ﴿Upon Him I have relied﴾ in my support against you (p-155) ﴿and to Him is my return﴾, my place of return, so that He will reward me for my patience with you. My return (mataban), my punishment (iqab) and my final abode (ma'ab): in both states, the grammatical form is ya'qub.

﴿وَلَوْ أنَّ قُرْآنًا سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ الجِبالُ﴾ عَنْ مَقارِّها ﴿أوْ قُطِّعَتْ بِهِ الأرْضُ﴾ حَتّى تَتَصَدَّعَ وتَتَزايَلَ قِطَعًا ﴿أوْ كُلِّمَ بِهِ المَوْتى﴾ فَتَسْمَعُ وتُجِيبُ، لَكانَ هَذا القُرْآنُ، لِكَوْنِهِ غايَةً في التَذْكِيرِ ونِهايَةً في الإنْذارِ والتَخْوِيفِ. فَجَوابُ لَوْ (jawab, the apodosis of the conditional) مَحْذُوفٌ، أوْ مَعْناهُ: ولَوْ أنَّ قُرْآنًا وقَعَ بِهِ تَسْيِيرُ الجِبالِ وتَقْطِيعُ الأرْضِ وتَكْلِيمُ المَوْتى وتَنْبِيئُهم لَما آمَنُوا بِهِ ولَما تَنَبَّهُوا عَلَيْهِ، كَقَوْلِهِ: ﴿وَلَوْ أنَّنا نَزَّلْنا إلَيْهِمُ المَلائِكَةَ﴾ الآيَةَ. ﴿بَلْ لِلَّهِ الأمْرُ جَمِيعًا﴾: بَلْ لِلَّهِ القُدْرَةُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، وهو قادِرٌ عَلى الآياتِ الَّتِي اقْتَرَحُوها. ﴿أفَلَمْ يَيْأسِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾: أفَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ، وهي لُغَةُ قَوْمٍ مِنَ النَخَعِ (Nakha', a tribe). وقِيلَ: إنَّما اسْتُعْمِلَ اليَأْسُ بِمَعْنى العِلْمِ لِتَضَمُّنِهِ مَعْناهُ، لِأنَّ اليائِسَ عَنِ الشَيْءِ عالِمٌ بِأنَّهُ لا يَكُونُ، كَما اسْتُعْمِلَ النِسْيانُ في مَعْنى التَرْكِ لِتَضَمُّنِ ذَلِكَ. دَلِيلُهُ قِراءَةُ عَلِيٍّ (رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ) "أفَلَمْ يَتَبَيَّنْ" (qira'a, a variant reading). وقِيلَ: إنَّما كَتَبَهُ الكاتِبُ وهو ناعِسٌ مُسْتَوِي السِناتِ، وهَذِهِ، وَاللهِ، فِرْيَةٌ ما فِيها مِرْيَةٌ!

﴿أنْ لَوْ يَشاءُ اللهُ لَهَدى الناسَ جَمِيعًا﴾ ﴿وَلا يَزالُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا تُصِيبُهم بِما صَنَعُوا﴾

مِن كُفْرِهِمْ وسُوءِ أعْمالِهِمْ ﴿قارِعَةٌ﴾: داهِيَةٌ تَقْرَعُهم بِما يُحِلُّ اللهُ بِهِمْ في كُلِّ وقْتٍ مِن صُنُوفِ البَلايا والمَصائِبِ في نُفُوسِهِمْ وأوْلادِهِمْ وأمْوالِهِمْ. ﴿أوْ تَحُلُّ قَرِيبًا مِن دارِهِمْ﴾: أوْ تَحُلُّ القارِعَةُ قَرِيبًا مِنهم فَيَفْزَعُونَ، ويَتَطايَرُ عَلَيْهِمْ شَرَرُها، ويَتَعَدّى إلَيْهِمْ شُرُورُها. ﴿حَتّى يَأْتِيَ وعْدُ اللهِ﴾: أيْ: مَوْتُهم، أوِ القِيامَةُ. أوْ: ولا يَزالُ كُفّارُ مَكَّةَ تُصِيبُهم بِما صَنَعُوا بِرَسُولِ اللهِ مِنَ العَداوَةِ والتَكْذِيبِ قارِعَةٌ، لِأنَّ جَيْشَ رَسُولِ اللهِ يُغِيرُ حَوْلَ مَكَّةَ ويَخْتَطِفُ مِنهم (p-١٥٦) أوْ تَحُلُّ أنْتَ يا مُحَمَّدُ قَرِيبًا مِن دارِهِمْ بِجَيْشِكَ يَوْمَ الحُدَيْبِيَةِ، حَتّى يَأْتِيَ وعْدُ اللهِ، أيْ: فَتْحُ مَكَّةَ. ﴿إنَّ اللهَ لا يُخْلِفُ المِيعادَ﴾: أيْ: لا خُلْفَ في مَوْعِدِهِ.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 32:

﴿And indeed, messengers before you were mocked, so I gave respite to those who disbelieved; then I seized them, and how was My punishment!﴾ Al-imla' (respite) means granting a delay, and that one be left for a long period (milawah) of time in ease and security. ﴿Then I seized them, and how was My punishment!﴾ This is a threat to them, and an answer concerning their demand for signs from the Messenger of Allah, mocking him, and a consolation for him.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 33:

﴿Is then He who stands over every soul in account of what it has earned⦆ (a rhetorical argument against them regarding their associating others with Allah). It means: Is then Allah, who is Watchful over every soul, whether righteous or wicked, in account of what it has earned, knowing its good and its evil and preparing for each its recompense, like one who is not so? Then he resumed, saying: ﴿And they have set up for Allah partners﴾, namely the idols. ﴿Say: Name them﴾, i.e., name for Him who they are, and inform Him of their names. Then he said: ﴿Or do you inform Him of what He does not know on the earth﴾, with "أم" here being disjunctive (munqati'ah), i.e., rather, do you inform Him of partners whom He does not know on the earth, while He is the Knower of what is in the heavens and the earth? So if He does not know them, it is known that they are nothing, and the intended meaning is the negation that He has any partners. ﴿Or with an outward saying?⦆ Rather, do you name them partners with an outward saying, without there being any reality to that, like His words: "That is their saying with their mouths" and "You worship besides Him only names which you have named"? ﴿Nay, the scheming of those who disbelieve has been made attractive to them⦆, i.e., their plotting against Islam by their associating others with Allah. ﴿And they have been turned away from the way⦆, from the way of Allah, with the ṣād vocalised with a ḍammah by Kūfan readers and with a fatḥah by others; its meaning is: and they turned the Muslims away from the way of Allah. ﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide⦆, i.e., no one who is able to guide him.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 34:

﴿For them there is a punishment in the life of this world﴾ by killing, capture, and various kinds of trials. ﴿But the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe﴾ (ashaqq), i.e., more intense, because of its perpetuity. ﴿And they will have no protector from Allah﴾ (min waq), i.e., no guardian from His punishment.

The Parable of Paradise promised to the God-fearing: its description, which is in the strangeness of the parable, and its being raised as a subject (mubtada'), with the predicate omitted, i.e., "in what is recited to you is the parable of Paradise." Or the predicate is ﴿Beneath which rivers flow﴾, as you would say, "the description of Zayd is 'dark-complexioned'." ﴿Its fruit is everlasting﴾: its fruit is of constant existence and does not cease. ﴿And its shade﴾ is everlasting and is not abrogated in this world by the sun. ﴿That is the final outcome of those who have been God-fearing﴾, i.e., the Paradise described is the outcome of their taqwa (God-consciousness), meaning the end of their affair. ﴿And the final outcome of the disbelievers is the Fire.﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 36:

﴿And those to whom We have given the Book﴾ means those of the Jews who embraced Islam, such as Ibn Salam (ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam) and others like him, and of the Christians in the land of Abyssinia. ﴿rejoice at what has been sent down to you﴾ ﴿and among the factions﴾ means: and among their factions, namely their disbelievers, who united against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in enmity, such as Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf and his companions, and al-Sayyid and al-ʿAqib and their partisans. ﴿who deny part of it﴾ because they did not deny the narratives (al-aqasis) and some of the rulings and meanings that are established in their books. They did deny the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and other matters among the laws that they had distorted and altered.

﴿Say: I have only been commanded to worship Allah and not associate anything with Him﴾. This is an answer to the deniers, meaning: Say, "I have only been commanded, in what has been sent down to me, to worship Allah and not to associate anything with Him." So their denial of it is a denial of the worship of Allah and His oneness. Look, then, at what you deny, while you yourselves claim that the worship of Allah is obligatory and that nothing should be associated with Him!

﴿To Him I call﴾, specifically; I do not call to other than Him. ﴿And to Him﴾, not to other than Him, ﴿is my return (ma'ab)﴾, my place of return. You also say the same thing, so there is no sense in your denial.

﴿And thus We sent it down﴾, meaning: in the same manner of sending down, We sent it down, commanding in it the worship of Allah and His Oneness, calling to Him and to His religion, and warning of the abode of recompense. ﴿A judgment in Arabic﴾: wisdom in Arabic, translated into the tongue of the Arabs. Its being in the accusative here is as a *hal* (circumstantial accusative). (p-158) The polytheists used to call the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to matters in which they would share with him, so it was said: ﴿And if you were to follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:145], meaning: after the knowledge had been established by decisive proofs and clear demonstrations. ﴿You would have against Allah no protector or defender﴾, meaning: no helper would support you, and no defender would shield you from Him. This is of the manner of stirring up and urging the listeners to firmness in the religion, and that no one who holds fast to the proof should slip when doubt arises. Otherwise, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in a station of utmost firmness.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 38:

They used to find fault with him (ﷺ) for marrying and having children, and they would demand signs from him, and they denied abrogation (naskh, the replacement of one ruling by another). So there was revealed: ﴿And We had already sent messengers before you and given them wives and offspring﴾, that is, women and children. ﴿And it was not for a messenger to bring a sign except by the permission of Allah﴾. That is: it is not within his power to bring signs according to what his people propose; rather, that is up to Allah. ﴿For every term there is a decree﴾, that is, for every time there is a ruling that is written (kitab) upon the servants, meaning it is imposed upon them according to what His wisdom requires.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 39:

﴿Allah erases what He wills﴾ — He abrogates (yansakh, "abrogation" = naskh) whatever He wills to abrogate. ﴿And establishes﴾ in its place whatever He wills, or leaves it unabrogated; or He erases from the register of the recording angels (diwan al-hafazah) whatever He wills and establishes something else; or He erases the disbelief of those who repent and establishes their faith in its place; or He causes to die whoever's term (ajal) has come and the reverse.

"Yuthabbit" (﴿وَيُثَبِّتُ﴾, "and establishes", with doubled ba') is read by the Medinan, the Syrian, Hamzah and Ali (Medinan = the reader of Medina, Shami = the reader of Syria, Hamzah and Ali are among the canonical readers).

﴿And with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾ — i.e., the origin (asl) of every book, which is the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz), because every existing thing is written in it.

﴿And whether We show you some of what We promise them or take you (in death)﴾ [Yunus: 46]. However the situation turned out, We showed you their places of downfall and what We had promised them of the descent of punishment upon them, or We took you (in death) before that. ﴿Your duty is only to convey (the message)﴾, meaning it is incumbent upon you only to convey the message, nothing more. ﴿And upon Us is the reckoning (p-159)﴾, meaning upon Us is their reckoning and their recompense for their deeds, not upon you. So let not their turning away distress you, and do not hasten (the coming of) their punishment.

﴿Have they not seen that We come to the land﴾, the land of the disbelievers, ﴿reducing it from its outskirts﴾ by what We open up for the Muslims of their lands. So We diminish the abode of war (dar al-harb) and increase the abode of Islam (dar al-Islam), and this is among the signs of victory and triumph. The meaning is: your duty is only the delivery of the message with which you have been charged, and do not concern yourself with what lies beyond that, for We will suffice you in it and complete what We have promised you of victory and success. ﴿And Allah judges; there is none to repel His judgment﴾, meaning none to turn back His judgment. The one who "reverses" (mu'aqqib) is the one who turns against a thing and nullifies it. Its real sense is one who follows (ya'qibuhu), that is, pursues it with rejection and nullification. From this comes the saying about the rightful creditor, "mu'aqqib", because he pursues his debtor with demand and insistence. The meaning is that it is a judgment in favour of Islam with victory and advancement, and against unbelief with retreat and reversal. The grammatical position (mahall) of "there is none to repel His judgment" is the accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal), as if it were said: "And Allah judges, His judgment being executed," just as you say, "Zayd came to me without a turban on his head and without a cap," meaning bareheaded. ﴿And He is swift in reckoning﴾, so He will call them to account in the Hereafter after the punishment of this world, and that will be soon.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verse 42:

﴿And those before them had indeed plotted⁠—﴾ that is, the disbelievers of the earlier nations against their prophets. Makr (plotting, scheming) is the intention of harm in secret, then their plotting was made as though it were no plotting in comparison with His plotting, so He said: ﴿So to Allah belongs all plotting.﴾ Then He explained that by His saying: ﴿He knows what every soul earns, and the disbelievers will know to whom belongs the ultimate abode.﴾ That is, the praiseworthy outcome. For whoever knows what every soul earns and prepares for it its recompense, his is the entire plotting, because it comes to them from where they do not perceive, while they are heedless of what is intended for them. "Al-kafir" (the disbeliever), taken in the generic sense, is read by Hijazi and Abu 'Amr.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 13, verse 43:**

﴿And those who disbelieve say, "You are not a messenger."﴾ Those meant are Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and the leaders of the Jews, who said, "You are not a messenger" for this reason. ʿAṭāʾ said: "It is Meccan (*makkiyya*, revealed in Mecca) except for this verse," namely ﴿Say: "Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you"﴾, by what He has manifested of the proofs of my prophethood. (p-160) The *bāʾ* (the preposition "by") entered upon the agent (*fāʿil*), and *shahīdan* (as a witness) is a *tamyīz* (specificative accusative, clarifying what is meant). ﴿And whoever has knowledge of the Book﴾: it was said that this is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and "the Book" is the Preserved Tablet (*al-lawḥ al-maḥfūẓ*). Its evidence is the reading of the one who read *"wa-min ʿindihi ʿilmu al-kitāb"* (وَمِن عِنْدِهِ عِلْمُ الكِتابِ), meaning "and from Him is the knowledge of the Book," because the knowledge of the one who knows it comes from His grace and kindness. It was also said that it refers to one of the scholars of the People of the Book who embraced Islam, because they bear witness to His description in their scriptures. Ibn Salām said: "This verse was revealed concerning me." It was also said that it refers to Jibrīl (Gabriel), peace be upon him. The word *man* (مَن, "whoever") is in the place of the genitive by coordination with the wording "Allah" (اللهِ), or in the place of the nominative by coordination with the position (*maḥall*) of the prepositional phrase, since the implied sense is "Allah is sufficient." The phrase *ʿilmu al-kitāb* (عِلْمُ الكِتابِ) takes the nominative by the implied verb within the adverbial phrase (*fī al-ẓarf*), so that it is the agent (*fāʿil*), because the adverbial phrase is the relative clause (*ṣila*) of *man*. Here *man* carries the meaning of *alladhī* (the one who), and the sense is: "whoever has the knowledge of the Book established with him." This is so because when the adverbial phrase falls as a relative clause it functions as a verb, as in your saying: *marartu bi-alladhī fī al-dār akhūhu* (I passed by the one who is in the house, his brother), where *akhūhu* (his brother) is the agent, just as you say: *bi-alladhī istaqarra fī al-dār akhūhu* (by the one whose brother settled in the house). In the reading with a kasra on the *mīm* of *min* (مِن), *al-ʿilm* (العِلْمُ, "the knowledge") is nominative by beginning (*ibtidāʾ*), with the beginning-with-beginning construction.
